messages:
Sanjay: Quick sync — I'm kicking off region bring-up for ap-southeast4 GPU cluster. Need agreement on Terraform vs Pulumi modules and remote state wiring. Plan idea: TF for cloud infra (VPC, subnet, node pools), Pulumi for runtime config (k8s, node labels). Any blockers with state/CI wiring?
Maya: +1 to single source per concern. Prefer TF for infra and keep Pulumi only for things that need imperative SDKs. Avoid cross-tool in-place state reads.
Eli: Pulumi Service backend is convenient but for Private deployments we should avoid it. If we use Pulumi OSS, keep state in the same backend family as TF (GCS for GCP) and enforce locking.
Rachel: Practical pattern we've used: TF outputs -> export to artifact (outputs.json) -> Pulumi reads that artifact in CI. Keeps states isolated and explicit.
Henry: strong 👍 on artifact approach. Avoid terraform_remote_state usage across workspaces; caused subtle race issues before. Use: `terraform output -json > tf_outputs.json` then upload.
Maya: For GCP remote state: GCS backend + object versioning off, uniform bucket-level access, CMEK for encryption. For locking we rely on build-level sequencing; terraform GCS doesn't have a native lock like S3+Dynamo. Use Terraform Cloud or a lock coordinator if needed.
Sanjay: For Private customers we need KMS-only secrets for Pulumi. Do we have a standard secrets provider string we can share?
Eli: Yes — for Pulumi OSS we use `--secrets-provider="gcpkms://projects/<proj>/locations/<loc>/keyRings/<kr>/cryptoKeys/<key>"`. For AWS KMS use `awskms://...` in similar fashion. Document per-customer override.
CI-bot: Pipeline template created: `pipelines/region-gpu.yaml`. Steps: `terraform-plan`, `terraform-apply`, `upload-outputs`, `pulumi-preview`, `pulumi-update`. See https://git.internal/pipelines/region-gpu-template
OPS-BOT: Reminder: after Pulumi success, run `register-region ap-southeast4 --tier dedicated` so fleet inventory and quotas reconcile.
Rachel: Validation checklist to add to runbook: nodepool size matches requested GPUs, GPU type (A100 vs H100) is correct, taints/labels set, nvidia device-plugin DS is Running, driver installer DaemonSet succeeded, and k8s node conditions OK. Also smoke test: submit trivial inference job and assert 95th pct latency <200ms.
Sanjay: Can someone paste a minimal CI snippet for outputs upload + Pulumi consume? Want copy/paste for the runbook.
Henry: Snippet:
```
# terraform pipeline step after apply
terraform output -json > tf_outputs.json
gsutil cp tf_outputs.json gs://redwood-region-artifacts/${REGION}/${BUILD_ID}/tf_outputs.json

# pulumi pipeline step
gsutil cp gs://redwood-region-artifacts/${REGION}/${BUILD_ID}/tf_outputs.json .
export TF_OUTPUTS=$(cat tf_outputs.json)
pulumi stack select ${PULUMI_STACK}
pulumi up --yes --secrets-provider="gcpkms://projects/.../locations/.../keyRings/.../cryptoKeys/..."
```
Maya: Also add a small validator job after Pulumi: `kubectl get ds nvidia-device-plugin -n kube-system -o yaml` and `curl -fsS http://internal-health/api/region || exit 1`. Include retry/backoff.
Eli: Cost note: ap-southeast4 preemptible GPUs are cheaper but not suitable for Dedicated SLA. Add a `cost-estimate` step in CI: `terraform plan -out=plan.out && terraform show -json plan.out | ./tools/estimate-costs` or use the cloud pricing API.
Sanjay: OK great — I'll draft the runbook with the artifact wiring pattern and the validation checklist. Will open a PR shortly. Thanks all :thumbsup:
